name: Extermination of the Inhabitants of Kishkeroy-Yurt by Pullo's Detachment: 76 Killed, 40 Captured, Village Burned with Its Stores (December 1836) (C1158)

techniques.comment: In the course of the extermination of Kishkeroy-Yurt on 28-31 December 1836, Pullo's detachment led away 40 inhabitants into captivity: "40 souls of both sexes were taken captive"(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959).

In the course of the extermination of Kishkeroy-Yurt, Pullo's detachment deliberately destroyed the winter stores: the village was burned "with a considerable stock of grain and hay," and the following day part of the detachment "was occupied with the destruction of the hay stored in the surrounding area"(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959). The destruction of grain and fodder stores in the depth of winter left the surviving inhabitants without means to survive it.

On 28 December 1836, during the sudden encirclement of Kishkeroy-Yurt, Pullo's troops killed inhabitants who tried to escape, as well as families in their houses: "those seeking salvation in flight were caught or exterminated", "the inhabitants, having barricaded themselves in their houses with their families, were put to the bayonet", and two were smoked out "by straw thrown into the chimneys"(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959). Upon the occupation of the village, 76 bodies of the slain were found(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959). Some of the inhabitants mounted an armed defense, and among the 76 killed are those who fell bearing arms; the technique is recorded on the basis of the killing of those fleeing and of families trapped in their houses.

In the course of the extermination of Kishkeroy-Yurt on 28-31 December 1836, Pullo's detachment appropriated the inhabitants' property, including weapons taken from the bodies of the slain: "all the property of the inhabitants and the weapons taken from the slain fell to our troops"(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959).

In late December 1836, Colonel Pullo carried out a punitive raid on the Chechen village of Kishkeroy-Yurt (Keshkeroy) beyond the Gudermes river, to punish its inhabitants for harboring Tashu-Hadji, the leader of the Chechen resistance. In April 1836, Nicholas I had demanded that action against Tashu-Hadji be undertaken "not otherwise than with complete confidence of success"(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том VIII (1831-1837) 1881), and on 10 December 1836 Rozen reported to the Minister of War Chernyshev that he "had authorized Col. Pullo to act at once against the unsubmissive Chechen villages"(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том VIII (1831-1837) 1881). Over the four days of the raid, the village was exterminated together with 76 inhabitants and defenders, and 40 people were led away into captivity(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959).

On 29-31 December 1836, Pullo's detachment completely destroyed Kishkeroy-Yurt: "the village of Kishkeroy, consisting of 63 households, with a considerable stock of grain and hay, was put to the torch", and on withdrawing on 31 December Pullo "marched out of Kishkeroy-Yurt, having set fire to the houses that remained undestroyed"(Citation: Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века: сборник документов 1959).
